target.title: fix(memory): recover from same-file legacy index divergence
target.body:
Related: #108532

Continues #109865. This supersedes that stalled PR because its contributor branch cannot be updated from this environment. Credit to @Serhii-Leniv for the original fix; the first three commits preserve Serhii Leniv's authorship.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with legacy and canonical Memory Core rows in the same per-agent SQLite database could enter a Gateway crash loop when rows shared an identity but held different values. In this state, `openclaw doctor --fix` could report success without repairing the database, and the next Gateway start failed again.

The original report is closed as #108532, but its [Docker reproduction and doctor evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108532#issuecomment-4987458050) show the same-file failure remained: the mounted `main.sqlite` kept conflicting after doctor ran and the Gateway still refused to start. This PR preserves that paper trail without reopening the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Summary

Same-file migration now treats existing canonical rows as authoritative, imports non-conflicting legacy-only rows, and drops the legacy tables only after proving every eligible identity is represented canonically. Chunk migration snapshots ownership before copying so stale chunks cannot be mixed into a source that already has a canonical chunk set. A partially migrated, chunkless source imports legacy chunks only when its source metadata still matches; divergent source metadata is removed so normal source sync must rebuild current content instead of accepting stale chunks.

The original migration tests were split into `memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts`, keeping both test files below the max-lines limit without a lint suppression or loss of migration-boundary coverage.

### Root Cause

On current `main`, the same-file migration's copied-row assertion compares full row values. When canonical and legacy `meta`, `files`, `chunks`, or `embedding_cache` rows have the same key but different values, it throws a plain `Error("legacy memory <table> rows conflict with canonical memory index rows")`.

That path is reached by Memory Core schema initialization during runtime startup and by doctor before doctor enters the sidecar-import recovery block. The recovery added in #108652 catches `LegacyMemoryDerivedRowsConflictError` from the sidecar import only, so it cannot recover this plain same-file error. The result matches #108532's observed Docker behavior: startup repeatedly fails while doctor leaves the same conflict in place.

This change uses SQLite's conflict-ignore behavior only for duplicate canonical identities, then verifies identity/source ownership explicitly before dropping legacy tables. Rows that cannot be represented by the canonical STRICT schema still fail closed and retain the legacy tables.

## User Impact

Memory Core can start again when an older same-file index contains stale values for keys already present in the canonical tables. Canonical indexed content wins, safe legacy-only content is retained, and repeating schema initialization is idempotent.

Genuinely uncopyable legacy rows—for example, values rejected by canonical STRICT constraints—still hard-fail. That residual recovery case is intentionally unchanged and remains follow-up work rather than being silently discarded here.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Proof environment: Linux source checkout, Node `v25.9.0`, real on-disk `DatabaseSync` files in WAL mode. The current-main baseline was `a9dc393f7eb84f515994789b8eefafa206e96914`; the patched head was `c0e42f72d35c99e4e08aa1b115e88ca77a5a1fb5`.

Each run began from an independently seeded state directory. The affected database lived at its real canonical path, `<state>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. That one file contained both canonical `memory_index_*` tables and the partially migrated legacy `meta`, `files`, `chunks`, and `embedding_cache` tables. Every legacy table had a row with the same identity but different values from its canonical counterpart, plus safe legacy-only rows. A normal `<state>/memory/main.sqlite` sidecar existed only to make the real startup/doctor state-migration path inspect the canonical target.

This reproduces the important mounted-state constraint: the divergent tables are inside the canonical agent database, so doctor cannot recover by renaming that database aside as a derived sidecar. No Docker daemon, container, bind mount, or OS-level rename denial was exercised; the canonical path and in-place schema state were reproduced on a normal local filesystem.

#### Current-main failure

Redacted transcript; `<proof-root>` replaces the temporary local path.

```text
$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs seed <proof-root>/main-case
{"seeded":true,"canonicalPath":"<state>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite","legacySidecarPath":"<state>/memory/main.sqlite","journalMode":"wal","partialMigration":true}

$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs inspect <proof-root>/main-case
journalMode=wal
legacyTables=[meta,files,chunks,embedding_cache]
memoryStateHash=37ed4c36ace6ba4730b8927e10237b8ad81e2d6b80c0e474c085a170150f51ae

$ HOME=<proof-root>/main-case/home \
    OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof-root>/main-case/state \
    OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<proof-root>/main-case/state/openclaw.json \
    NO_COLOR=1 node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port <port> --bind loopback --auth none
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Skipped Memory Core legacy memory index import for agent main because the sidecar could not be imported: Error: legacy memory meta rows conflict with canonical memory index rows
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
exit=1

$ HOME=<proof-root>/main-case/home \
    OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof-root>/main-case/state \
    OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<proof-root>/main-case/state/openclaw.json \

└  Doctor complete.

$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs inspect <proof-root>/main-case
journalMode=wal
legacyTables=[meta,files,chunks,embedding_cache]
canonical MEMORY.md hash=canonical-file-hash; legacy MEMORY.md hash=legacy-file-hash
canonical same-chunk text="canonical memory remains authoritative"; legacy same-chunk text="legacy divergent text"
canonical same-key cache=[1,0,0]@200; legacy same-key cache=[0,1,0]@100
sidecarPresent=true; sidecarArchived=false
memoryStateHash=37ed4c36ace6ba4730b8927e10237b8ad81e2d6b80c0e474c085a170150f51ae

$ HOME=<proof-root>/main-case/home \
    OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof-root>/main-case/state \
    OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<proof-root>/main-case/state/openclaw.json \
    NO_COLOR=1 node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port <port> --bind loopback --auth none
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Skipped Memory Core legacy memory index import for agent main because the sidecar could not be imported: Error: legacy memory meta rows conflict with canonical memory index rows
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
exit=1
```

Thus current main reproduced all three reported behaviors: Gateway refused readiness, doctor exited successfully without repairing the memory state, and the next Gateway invocation failed identically. The row-level memory-state hash before and after doctor was the same.

#### Patched behavior

The PR head started from an identically seeded fresh fixture.

```text
$ HOME=<proof-root>/branch-case/home \
    OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof-root>/branch-case/state \
    OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<proof-root>/branch-case/state/openclaw.json \
    NO_COLOR=1 node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port <port> --bind loopback --auth none
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
- Migrated Memory Core legacy memory index for agent main -> per-agent SQLite (1 source(s), 1 chunk(s), 1 cache row(s))
- Archived Memory Core legacy memory index sidecar -> <proof-root>/branch-case/state/memory/main.sqlite.migrated
[gateway] ready

$ curl --silent --show-error --fail --write-out '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/readyz
{"ready":true,"failing":[],"uptimeMs":17739,"eventLoop":{"degraded":true,"reasons":["event_loop_delay"],"intervalMs":17739,"delayP99Ms":21.4,"delayMaxMs":2868.9,"utilization":0.212,"cpuCoreRatio":0.362}}
HTTP 200

$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs inspect <proof-root>/branch-case
journalMode=wal
legacyTables=[]
canonical MEMORY.md hash=canonical-file-hash
canonical same-chunk text="canonical memory remains authoritative"
canonical same-key cache=[1,0,0]@200
retainedRows=[LEGACY_ONLY.md,legacy-only-chunk,legacy-only-key,SIDECAR.md,sidecar-chunk,sidecar-key]
sidecarPresent=false; sidecarArchived=true
memoryStateHash=2cd83c0e3834333214f469adfe949259dad02f82b12b1ac569da19bf5a163b76

$ HOME=<proof-root>/branch-case/home \
    OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof-root>/branch-case/state \
    OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<proof-root>/branch-case/state/openclaw.json \
    NO_COLOR=1 node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
# no Memory Core legacy-state detection, migration warning, or repair
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0

$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs inspect <proof-root>/branch-case
memoryStateHash=2cd83c0e3834333214f469adfe949259dad02f82b12b1ac569da19bf5a163b76

$ HOME=<proof-root>/branch-case/home \
    OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof-root>/branch-case/state \
    OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<proof-root>/branch-case/state/openclaw.json \
    NO_COLOR=1 node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port <port> --bind loopback --auth none
[gateway] ready
$ curl --silent --show-error --fail --write-out '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/readyz
{"ready":true,"failing":[],"uptimeMs":30570,"eventLoop":{"degraded":true,"reasons":["event_loop_delay"],"intervalMs":30570,"delayP99Ms":21.2,"delayMaxMs":1210.1,"utilization":0.071,"cpuCoreRatio":0.117}}

$ HOME=<proof-root>/branch-case/home \

    NO_COLOR=1 node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
# again no Memory Core legacy-state detection, migration warning, or repair
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0
$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs inspect <proof-root>/branch-case
memoryStateHash=2cd83c0e3834333214f469adfe949259dad02f82b12b1ac569da19bf5a163b76
```

The startup path repaired the same-file partial migration in place. Canonical divergent values won, safe legacy-only rows survived, all four same-file legacy tables were removed, Gateway readiness succeeded twice, and two doctor runs left the repaired memory state unchanged. Doctor also reported unrelated local-environment diagnostics (for example, no configured command owner and no installed user Gateway service); those are outside this Memory Core migration and did not affect exit status or readiness proof.

### Verification

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
```

```text
$ pnpm format packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts
$ git diff --check
# all clean
```

Mandatory autoreview was rerun after addressing all actionable findings:

```text
$ .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
```

### What was not tested

- No Docker daemon/container or real bind-mounted filesystem was used. This proof exercised the reported canonical path, WAL mode, partially migrated same-file schema, actual Gateway startup gate, actual readiness endpoint, actual `doctor --fix`, and repeated-run idempotence on the local filesystem.
- No packaged install, full test suite, or cross-platform run was performed. The source CLI rebuilt and ran successfully on both exact SHAs; the production schema module and both touched test files retain the focused verification above.
